discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can turn an ordinary band insulator into a new state of matter, the quantum spin Hall insulator. It is protected by time-reversal symmetry and classified by a Z2 topological invariant. Their simple, transparent model generalised quantum Hall physics to zero magnetic field. It made a sharp prediction: counter-propagating helical edge states that give quantised conductance. In 2007 Molenkamp's group realised this in HgTe quantum wells, measuring the predicted 2e^2/h edge conductance. That turned an abstract Berry-phase concept into a measurable phenomenon. The theory and the experiment together launched the field of topological insulators, which extends to three-dimensional materials, topological superconductivity and the quantum anomalous Hall effect. It reshaped how condensed-matter physicists classify electronic phases, and it now sets the agenda for hundreds of groups worldwide.
